subject: Follow-up: DPA role split, subprocessors & breach-notify — HealthSync discovery
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@healthsync.co>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@healthsync.co>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: DPA role split, subprocessors & breach-notify — HealthSync discovery

Thanks again for your time this morning, Aisha and Tom — good conversation. Per our discovery, I captured the action items below specific to data handling / privacy asks so we can keep procurement moving: 

- HealthSync asks to confirm: will Redwood be a processor for routed customer data and never act as a controller for customer-provided PII? (short answer requested for procurement team)
- Subprocessor list & notify window: HealthSync requires a list of current subprocessors and a 30-day advanced notice for adding subprocessor with a right-to-object window (30 days).
- Breach notification timing: HealthSync needs confirmation of investigator timeline + notification window for incidents involving customer data (they prefer 48 hrs for initial notification).
- Data residency & retention: confirm options for EU residency (if/when required) and recommended retention defaults for logs/metrics.

Next steps we agreed on:
1) I will loop in Legal to provide a short memo addressing controller/processor stance and our proposed breach-notify SLAs.
2) Laura will attach the most recent DPA and highlight the subprocessor clause.
3) We'll submit a marked-up DPA for your redlines and provide a DocuSign link for signature once both sides agree.

Attachments: redwood_dpa_v3.pdf (current standard DPA).

If anything above is off, flag it — otherwise expect Laura's note with legal language later today.

Best,
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@healthsync.co>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@healthsync.co>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: DPA role split, subprocessors & breach-notify — HealthSync discovery

Monica — thanks for the recap. A couple of clarifying points from our security/procurement side before your legal team replies: 

- Controller/Processor: HealthSync's posture is that we are the controller for patient data; any vendor processing patient-identifiable data must sign a Processor DPA. We need explicit language that Redwood will not assert any controller role for HealthSync-sent data and that Redwood's processing is only to provide the inference service.
- Subprocessors: Please provide (1) current subprocessor list, (2) confirm the 30-day notice + right-to-object window we discussed, and (3) confirm whether subprocessors have access to raw request/response payloads or only operational telemetry.
- Breach notify: HealthSync standard is initial notification within 48 hours of confirming unauthorized access affecting customer data. Is that achievable? If Redwood requires a longer investigative timeline, please state the standard initial notification cadence and what data you'll include in the initial alert.
- Logs & retention: we need a short summary of retention periods for request logs, KV cache metadata, and whether we can configure purge windows per customer.

Tom and I will compile the legal redlines after Laura sends the DPA. We try to keep negotiation items narrow to speed procurement.

Regards,
Aisha Khan
Head of Security & Compliance, HealthSync
aisha.khan@healthsync.co
+1 (617) 555-2201

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@healthsync.co>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@healthsync.co>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: DPA role split, subprocessors & breach-notify — HealthSync discovery

Aisha — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, followed by attachments and a proposed next-step: a one-page memo + marked-up DPA attached.

1) Controller vs Processor: Redwood will act solely as a processor for HealthSync-provided customer data in the context of the inference service. We will not assert controller status in the DPA language. Our standard clause is included in the attached DPA (see section 2: Roles).

2) Subprocessors: attached is our current subprocessor list (embedded in DPA Exhibit A). We can commit to a 30-day notice prior to onboarding a new subprocessor and a 30-day right-to-object window. For operational clarity: subprocessors that run inference (hosting/GPUs) do have access to request/response payloads as necessary to provide the service; monitoring/metrics-only vendors have telemetry access only. We'll highlight that distinction in Exhibit A.

3) Breach notification: Redwood's standard practice is initial notification within 72 hours of confirmed unauthorized access that materially affects customer data. We understand HealthSync prefers 48 hours; we'll note HealthSync's preference in the DPA and propose a 72-hour initial notification with escalation commitments (e.g., immediate acknowledgement and interim status updates within 24 hours of our initial contact). If HealthSync needs contractual 48-hour initial notice, we can treat that as a negotiation point tied to SLA/price.

4) Logs & retention: default retention for request logs is 90 days; KV cache metadata is retained for 7 days by default (configurable with dedicated/private deployments). We can provide per-customer retention controls on Redwood Dedicated or Private deployments; for Hosted we can offer configurable retention via contract up to 365 days for logs subject to pricing and operational review.

Attachments: 1) marked-up DPA: HealthSync_markedup_DPA_v1.pdf (we've highlighted the processor language, subprocessor notice clause, and breach-notify section); 2) our clean DPA (redwood_dpa_v3.pdf). Also linking a short one-page memo that summarizes the position and suggested fallback options.

Proposed next step: review the attached marked DPA and tell us which of the three breach-notify options you'd prefer (48 contractual / 72 contractual with accelerated interim updates / 72 contractual + price credit). If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute legal-to-legal call tomorrow.

Thanks — Laura Bennett
Deputy General Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

---

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@healthsync.co>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@healthsync.co>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 15:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: DPA role split, subprocessors & breach-notify — HealthSync discovery

Laura — appreciate the clear and practical options. Quick replies: 

- Controller/Processor: confirmed — the wording in section 2 looks acceptable at a glance; we'll formalize any editorial redlines.
- Subprocessor notice & access: 30-day notice with right-to-object is fine. Please add explicit language that any subprocessor with access to raw request/response must be listed as a "processing subprocessor" in Exhibit A.
- Breach notify: HealthSync preference is contractual 48-hour initial notification. We understand Redwood's 72-hour model; this will be a deal negotiator item. Can you flag whether there are operational blockers to committing to 48 hours for Hosted customers? If this is only available on Dedicated/Private tiers, note that in the memo.
- Retention: 90 days default for hosted is workable. We'll follow up on options/cost for 365-day retention for logs.

We'll compile redlines and send them via DocuSign once we agree on breach-notify language. For now, please add the explicit subprocessor-access distinction and indicate whether 48-hour notify is operationally feasible for Hosted.

Thanks — I'll aim to get initial redlines by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Aisha Khan
Head of Security & Compliance, HealthSync
